name: Intra-frame Prediction Analysis
description: Examines H.264/H.265 intra-frame prediction mode distributions — deepfake re-encoding alters prediction patterns.
mechanism:
This method analyzes H.264/H.265 intra-prediction patterns for video forensic detection:

1. **Intra-Prediction Mode Extraction**: For I-frames and intra-blocks in P/B-frames, the selected intra-prediction modes are extracted from the bitstream (9 modes in H.264, 35+ in H.265: DC, planar, and angular predictions). These mode decisions are influenced by local image content.

2. **Mode Distribution Analysis**: The statistical distribution of intra-prediction modes across the frame is analyzed. Natural video produces characteristic mode distributions — predominantly DC/planar in smooth regions, angular modes following edge orientations. Manipulated or AI-generated content may show anomalous mode distributions inconsistent with the visual content.

3. **Mode-Content Consistency**: The selected mode should match the actual image content direction. At a horizontal edge, a horizontal prediction mode should be selected. The method checks mode-content alignment — content inserted from a different encoding may show suboptimal mode selections (modes chosen for the original content, not the replaced content).

4. **Prediction Residual Analysis**: The intra-prediction residual (actual − predicted) encodes what the prediction couldn't capture. Residual statistics differ between original content (well-predicted, small residuals) and replaced content (poorly predicted by modes chosen for different content, larger residuals). The method detects anomalous residual distributions.

5. **Re-Encoding Signature Detection**: Double-encoded video (original + manipulation + re-encoding) shows characteristic intra-prediction artifacts: the second encoder's mode decisions partially align with the first encoder's block structure, creating detectable periodicity in prediction residuals.
parameters: Analysis type: automated statistical\nScore range: 0 (authentic) to 100 (AI-generated)\nMinimum input size: varies by media type
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-85% accuracy depending on input quality and method combination.
source: Based on peer-reviewed research in digital forensics and AI content detection.
useCase: Used as part of multi-signal analysis pipeline to detect AI-generated content.
strengths:
• Research-backed methodology
• Fast computation time
• Complementary to other detection methods
• Works across different AI generators
limitations: • Accuracy varies with input quality\n• Best used in combination with other methods\n• May require calibration for new AI models
